```python
print("\n" + "="*80)
print("ADVANCED COMPUTER VISION: COMPLETE SPECIALIZATION")
print("="*80)

print("""
👁️ TRACK B OVERVIEW: STATE-OF-THE-ART VISION

Topics Covered:
   184-188: Advanced Detection & Segmentation (5 topics)
   189-193: Modern Architectures (5 topics)
   194-198: Multimodal & 3D Vision (5 topics)
   199-203: Production CV (5 topics)

🎯 TOPICS 184-188: ADVANCED DETECTION & SEGMENTATION

TOPIC 184: YOLO EVOLUTION (v5-v8)

YOLOv5 (2020):
   • PyTorch native
   • Easy to train
   • Multiple sizes (n, s, m, l, x)
   • 140 FPS on V100

YOLOv7 (2022):
   • E-ELAN architecture
   • Compound scaling
   • State-of-the-art accuracy + speed

YOLOv8 (2023 - Ultralytics):
   • Anchor-free
   • Unified framework
   • Classification, detection, segmentation
   • Easy API

from ultralytics import YOLO

# Load model
model = YOLO('yolov8n.pt')  # nano

# Train
model.train(data='coco.yaml', epochs=100, imgsz=640)

# Inference
results = model('image.jpg')

# Results
for r in results:
    boxes = r.boxes  # Boxes object
    masks = r.masks  # Masks object (segmentation)
    probs = r.probs  # Class probabilities

# Export
model.export(format='onnx')  # ONNX, TensorRT, etc.

TOPIC 185: MODERN OBJECT DETECTION

DETR (DEtection TRansformer):
   • Set prediction (no NMS!)
   • Transformer encoder-decoder
   • Hungarian matching loss
   • Simpler pipeline

Advantages:
   ✅ No anchors
   ✅ No NMS
   ✅ End-to-end
   ✅ Flexible

from transformers import DetrImageProcessor, DetrForObjectDetection

processor = DetrImageProcessor.from_pretrained("facebook/detr-resnet-50")
model = DetrForObjectDetection.from_pretrained("facebook/detr-resnet-50")

inputs = processor(images=image, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)

# Post-process
target_sizes = torch.tensor([image.size[::-1]])
results = processor.post_process_object_detection(
    outputs, target_sizes=target_sizes
)[0]

Detectron2 (Facebook):
   • Modular framework
   • Many models: Faster R-CNN, Mask R-CNN, RetinaNet
   • Production-ready

from detectron2.engine import DefaultPredictor
from detectron2.config import get_cfg

cfg = get_cfg()
cfg.merge_from_file("configs/COCO-Detection/faster_rcnn_R_50_FPN_3x.yaml")
cfg.MODEL.WEIGHTS = "model_final.pth"

predictor = DefaultPredictor(cfg)
outputs = predictor(image)

TOPIC 186: ADVANCED SEGMENTATION

Semantic Segmentation:
   • Pixel-wise classification
   • One class per pixel

Instance Segmentation:
   • Detect + segment each instance
   • Mask R-CNN, YOLACT, SOLOv2

Panoptic Segmentation:
   • Semantic + Instance
   • Complete scene understanding
   • Panoptic FPN, UPSNet

Mask2Former (2022):
   • Universal segmentation
   • Semantic, instance, panoptic
   • Transformer-based
   • State-of-the-art!

from transformers import Mask2FormerImageProcessor, Mask2FormerForUniversalSegmentation

processor = Mask2FormerImageProcessor.from_pretrained("facebook/mask2former-swin-base-coco-instance")
model = Mask2FormerForUniversalSegmentation.from_pretrained("facebook/mask2former-swin-base-coco-instance")

inputs = processor(images=image, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)

# Post-process
result = processor.post_process_instance_segmentation(outputs, target_sizes=...)[0]

TOPIC 187: SEGMENT ANYTHING MODEL (SAM)

Meta's SAM (2023):
   • Promptable segmentation
   • Zero-shot generalization
   • 1 billion masks dataset

Prompts:
   • Points: Click on object
   • Boxes: Draw bounding box
   • Masks: Refine existing mask
   • Text: (with additional models)

from segment_anything import sam_model_registry, SamPredictor

sam = sam_model_registry["vit_h"](checkpoint="sam_vit_h.pth")
predictor = SamPredictor(sam)

# Set image
predictor.set_image(image)

# Prompt with point
input_point = np.array([[500, 375]])
input_label = np.array([1])  # 1=foreground

masks, scores, logits = predictor.predict(
    point_coords=input_point,
    point_labels=input_label,
    multimask_output=True
)

Applications:
   ✅ Interactive segmentation
   ✅ Data annotation
   ✅ Image editing
   ✅ Medical imaging

TOPIC 188: KEYPOINT DETECTION & POSE ESTIMATION

2D Pose Estimation:
   • Detect human keypoints
   • OpenPose, HRNet, ViTPose

3D Pose Estimation:
   • 3D coordinates from 2D image
   • SMPL, VIBE

Applications:
   ✅ Sports analysis
   ✅ Animation
   ✅ Action recognition
   ✅ AR/VR

OpenPose-style:
   • Bottom-up: Detect all keypoints → group
   • Top-down: Detect person → keypoints

MediaPipe Pose:
from mediapipe import solutions
from mediapipe.python.solutions import pose as mp_pose

pose = mp_pose.Pose()
results = pose.process(image)

for landmark in results.pose_landmarks.landmark:
    print(landmark.x, landmark.y, landmark.z)

🏗️ TOPICS 189-193: MODERN ARCHITECTURES

TOPIC 189: VISION TRANSFORMERS (ViT) DEEP DIVE

Architecture:
   1. Split image into patches (16×16)
   2. Linear projection of patches
   3. Add positional embeddings
   4. Standard Transformer encoder
   5. [CLS] token for classification

from transformers import ViTForImageClassification

model = ViTForImageClassification.from_pretrained('google/vit-base-patch16-224')

Key Findings:
   ✅ Match CNN performance (with enough data)
   ✅ Better transfer learning
   ✅ More interpretable
   ✅ Better scaling

Variants:
   • DeiT: Data-efficient training
   • BEiT: BERT-style pre-training
   • MAE: Masked autoencoder

TOPIC 190: SWIN TRANSFORMER

Hierarchical Vision Transformer:
   • Shifted windows
   • Multi-scale features
   • More efficient than ViT

Shifted Window Attention:
   • Local attention in windows
   • Shift windows between layers
   • Enables cross-window connections

Advantages:
   ✅ Linear complexity (vs quadratic)
   ✅ Hierarchical features (like CNNs)
   ✅ Better for dense prediction
   ✅ State-of-the-art across tasks

TOPIC 191: CONVNEXT

Modern CNN Design:
   • Apply Transformer ideas to CNNs
   • Depthwise convolutions
   • Larger kernels (7×7)
   • GELU activation
   • Layer normalization

Result: Match Transformer performance!

Lesson: It's not architecture, it's the training!

import timm

model = timm.create_model('convnext_base', pretrained=True)

TOPIC 192: EFFICIENT ARCHITECTURES

EfficientNet-V2:
   • NAS + Scaling
   • Fused-MBConv blocks
   • Progressive learning
   • Fast training

MobileNet-V3:
   • Neural architecture search
   • Hard swish activation
   • Squeeze-and-excitation
   • Mobile-optimized

ShuffleNet:
   • Channel shuffle
   • Depthwise convolutions
   • Very efficient

Comparison (ImageNet):
┌──────────────┬────────┬────────┬──────┐
│ Model        │ Top-1  │ Params │ FLOPs│
├──────────────┼────────┼────────┼──────┤

└──────────────┴────────┴────────┴──────┘

TOPIC 193: SELF-SUPERVISED LEARNING FOR VISION

Methods:

1. Contrastive Learning:
   • SimCLR, MoCo, SwAV
   • Pull similar images together
   • Push different images apart

2. Masked Image Modeling:
   • MAE (Masked Autoencoder)
   • Mask patches, reconstruct
   • Like BERT for images

3. DINO (Self-distillation):
   • Student-teacher framework
   • No labels needed
   • Learns semantic features

Benefits:
   ✅ Learn from unlabeled data
   ✅ Better representations
   ✅ Transfer learning

# Using DINO features
from transformers import ViTFeatureExtractor, ViTModel

extractor = ViTFeatureExtractor.from_pretrained('facebook/dino-vitb16')
model = ViTModel.from_pretrained('facebook/dino-vitb16')

inputs = extractor(images=image, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)
features = outputs.last_hidden_state

🌐 TOPICS 194-198: MULTIMODAL & 3D VISION

TOPIC 194: CLIP (CONTRASTIVE LANGUAGE-IMAGE PRE-TRAINING)

Training:
   • 400M image-text pairs
   • Contrastive loss
   • Align vision and language

Usage:
   • Zero-shot classification
   • Image-text retrieval
   • Text-to-image search

from transformers import CLIPProcessor, CLIPModel

model = CLIPModel.from_pretrained("openai/clip-vit-base-patch32")
processor = CLIPProcessor.from_pretrained("openai/clip-vit-base-patch32")

# Zero-shot classification
inputs = processor(
    text=["a photo of a cat", "a photo of a dog"],
    images=image,
    return_tensors="pt",
    padding=True
)

outputs = model(**inputs)
logits_per_image = outputs.logits_per_image
probs = logits_per_image.softmax(dim=1)

Applications:
   ✅ Zero-shot classification
   ✅ Image search
   ✅ Content moderation
   ✅ DALL-E, Stable Diffusion use CLIP!

TOPIC 195: VISION-LANGUAGE MODELS

Models:
   • CLIP (image-text matching)
   • BLIP (captioning + QA + retrieval)
   • Flamingo (few-shot vision-language)
   • LLaVA (Visual instruction tuning)
   • GPT-4V (vision capabilities)

BLIP Example:
from transformers import BlipProcessor, BlipForConditionalGeneration

processor = BlipProcessor.from_pretrained("Salesforce/blip-image-captioning-base")
model = BlipForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained("Salesforce/blip-image-captioning-base")

inputs = processor(image, return_tensors="pt")
out = model.generate(**inputs)
caption = processor.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True)

Visual Question Answering:
from transformers import BlipForQuestionAnswering

model = BlipForQuestionAnswering.from_pretrained("Salesforce/blip-vqa-base")
inputs = processor(image, text="What color is the car?", return_tensors="pt")
out = model.generate(**inputs)
answer = processor.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True)

TOPIC 196: TEXT-TO-IMAGE GENERATION

Evolution:
   • GANs: StyleGAN, BigGAN
   • Diffusion: DALL-E 2, Stable Diffusion, Imagen
   • Current SOTA: Diffusion models

Stable Diffusion:
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline

pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
    "stabilityai/stable-diffusion-2-1",
    torch_dtype=torch.float16
).to("cuda")

prompt = "A beautiful sunset over mountains, digital art"
image = pipe(prompt).images[0]

Advanced Features:
   • Image-to-image
   • Inpainting
   • ControlNet (guided generation)
   • DreamBooth (personalization)
   • LoRA (fine-tuning)

ControlNet Example:
from diffusers import ControlNetModel, StableDiffusionControlNetPipeline

controlnet = ControlNetModel.from_pretrained("lllyasviel/sd-controlnet-canny")
pipe = StableDiffusionControlNetPipeline.from_pretrained(
    "runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5",
    controlnet=controlnet
)

# Generate with edge map guidance
image = pipe(prompt, canny_image).images[0]

TOPIC 197: 3D VISION & NEURAL RADIANCE FIELDS

Point Clouds:
   • 3D coordinate data
   • LiDAR, depth sensors
   • PointNet, PointNet++

Depth Estimation:
from transformers import DPTImageProcessor, DPTForDepthEstimation

processor = DPTImageProcessor.from_pretrained("Intel/dpt-large")
model = DPTForDepthEstimation.from_pretrained("Intel/dpt-large")

inputs = processor(images=image, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)
depth = outputs.predicted_depth

NeRF (Neural Radiance Fields):
   • Represent 3D scene as neural network
   • Novel view synthesis
   • Photorealistic rendering

Applications:
   ✅ VR/AR
   ✅ 3D reconstruction
   ✅ Autonomous vehicles
   ✅ Robotics

TOPIC 198: VIDEO UNDERSTANDING

Challenges:
   • Temporal information
   • Computational cost
   • Long-range dependencies

Approaches:

1. 3D CNNs:
   • I3D, C3D
   • Spatial + temporal convolutions

2. Two-Stream Networks:
   • RGB stream + Optical flow stream
   • Fusion for prediction

3. Video Transformers:
   • TimeSFormer, ViViT
   • Attention across space and time

Action Recognition:
from transformers import VideoMAEForVideoClassification

model = VideoMAEForVideoClassification.from_pretrained("MCG-NJU/videomae-base-finetuned-kinetics")

# Video as tensor (batch, frames, channels, H, W)
outputs = model(video_tensor)
predicted_label = outputs.logits.argmax(-1)

🔧 TOPICS 199-203: PRODUCTION CV

TOPIC 199: MODEL OPTIMIZATION FOR CV

Techniques:

1. Quantization:
   • Post-training quantization (PTQ)
   • Quantization-aware training (QAT)
   • INT8 inference

import torch.quantization

model_quantized = torch.quantization.quantize_dynamic(
    model, {torch.nn.Linear, torch.nn.Conv2d}, dtype=torch.qint8
)

2. Pruning:
   • Remove unimportant weights
   • Structured vs unstructured

3. Knowledge Distillation:
   • Teacher-student training
   • Smaller model, similar performance

4. TensorRT:
   • NVIDIA inference optimizer
   • 10× speedup possible

5. ONNX:
   • Framework-agnostic
   • Cross-platform

# Export to ONNX
torch.onnx.export(
    model,
    dummy_input,
    "model.onnx",
    input_names=['input'],
    output_names=['output'],
    dynamic_axes={'input': {0: 'batch'}, 'output': {0: 'batch'}}
)

TOPIC 200: DATA AUGMENTATION ADVANCED

Techniques:

1. AutoAugment:
   • Learned augmentation policies
   • Search for best transformations

2. RandAugment:
   • Random magnitude
   • Simpler than AutoAugment

3. CutMix:
   • Cut and paste regions
   • Mix labels proportionally

4. MixUp:
   • Blend two images
   • Linear combination of labels

5. Albumentations:
   • Fast augmentation library
   • Many transformations

import albumentations as A

transform = A.Compose([
    A.RandomRotate90(),
    A.Flip(),
    A.Transpose(),
    A.OneOf([
        A.GaussNoise(),
        A.GaussianBlur(),
    ], p=0.2),
    A.OneOf([
        A.OpticalDistortion(),
        A.GridDistortion(),
    ], p=0.2),
    A.HueSaturationValue(p=0.3),
])

augmented = transform(image=image)['image']

TOPIC 201: ACTIVE LEARNING FOR CV

Concept:
   • Label most informative samples
   • Reduce annotation cost
   • Iterative improvement

Strategies:

1. Uncertainty Sampling:
   • Label samples with lowest confidence

2. Diversity Sampling:
   • Label diverse samples
   • Cover feature space

3. Expected Model Change:
   • Label samples that change model most

Pipeline:
   1. Train initial model
   2. Select informative samples
   3. Get labels
   4. Retrain model
   5. Repeat

Tools:
   • modAL
   • Alipy
   • Custom implementation

TOPIC 202: WEAKLY SUPERVISED LEARNING

Use Cases:
   • Expensive annotations
   • Image-level labels for detection
   • Noisy labels

Techniques:

1. Class Activation Mapping (CAM):
   • Localize objects with image labels
   • Grad-CAM, Score-CAM

2. Multiple Instance Learning:
   • Bag-level labels
   • Instance-level predictions

3. Pseudo-labeling:
   • Model generates labels
   • Retrain with pseudo-labels

4. Noisy Student:
   • Teacher-student framework
   • Add noise to student

TOPIC 203: CV DEPLOYMENT BEST PRACTICES

Pipeline:
   1. Model training
   2. Export (ONNX, TensorRT)
   3. Optimization (quantization, pruning)
   4. Containerization (Docker)
   5. Serving (FastAPI, TorchServe)
   6. Monitoring

FastAPI CV API:
from fastapi import FastAPI, File, UploadFile
from PIL import Image
import io

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/detect")
async def detect_objects(file: UploadFile = File(...)):
    # Read image
    contents = await file.read()
    image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(contents))
    
    # Inference
    results = model(image)
    
    # Format response
    detections = []
    for box in results.boxes:
        detections.append({
            "class": box.cls,
            "confidence": box.conf,
            "bbox": box.xyxy.tolist()
        })
    
    return {"detections": detections}

Optimization Checklist:
   ☐ Quantization (INT8)
   ☐ Batch inference
   ☐ Model caching
   ☐ GPU utilization
   ☐ Async processing
   ☐ Request queuing
   ☐ Auto-scaling

TorchServe:
   • Production-ready serving
   • Multi-model serving
   • Metrics, logging
   • A/B testing

torch-model-archiver \\
    --model-name resnet18 \\
    --version 1.0 \\
```

sections.title: Topic 204: User-Based Collaborative Filtering
sections.body:
**Concept:**
"Users who agreed in the past will agree in the future"
- Find similar users
- Recommend items those users liked

**Steps:**
1. Build user-item matrix
2. Compute user similarity
3. Find k nearest neighbors
4. Predict ratings based on neighbors

```python
# User-Based Collaborative Filtering
class UserBasedCF:
    """User-Based Collaborative Filtering"""
    
    def __init__(self, k=5):
        self.k = k  # Number of neighbors
        self.user_similarity = None
        self.user_item_matrix = None
    
    def fit(self, user_item_matrix):
        """
        Train the model.
        user_item_matrix: pandas DataFrame (users × items)
        """
        self.user_item_matrix = user_item_matrix
        
        # Compute user similarity (cosine similarity)
        self.user_similarity = cosine_similarity(user_item_matrix.fillna(0))
        
        # Convert to DataFrame for easier access
        self.user_similarity = pd.DataFrame(
            self.user_similarity,
            index=user_item_matrix.index,
            columns=user_item_matrix.index
        )
    
    def predict(self, user_id, item_id):
        """Predict rating for user-item pair"""
        if user_id not in self.user_item_matrix.index:
            return self.user_item_matrix[item_id].mean()  # Global average
        
        if item_id not in self.user_item_matrix.columns:
            return self.user_item_matrix.loc[user_id].mean()  # User average
        
        # Find k most similar users who rated this item
        similar_users = self.user_similarity[user_id].sort_values(ascending=False)
        similar_users = similar_users[similar_users.index != user_id]  # Exclude self
        
        # Get users who rated this item
        rated_users = self.user_item_matrix[item_id].dropna().index
        similar_and_rated = similar_users[similar_users.index.isin(rated_users)]
        
        if len(similar_and_rated) == 0:
            return self.user_item_matrix[item_id].mean()
        
        # Get top k neighbors
        top_k = similar_and_rated.head(self.k)
        
        # Weighted average of their ratings
        weights = top_k.values
        ratings = self.user_item_matrix.loc[top_k.index, item_id].values
        
        if weights.sum() == 0:
            return ratings.mean()
        
        predicted = np.dot(weights, ratings) / weights.sum()
        return predicted
    
    def recommend(self, user_id, n=10):
        """Get top N recommendations for user"""
        if user_id not in self.user_item_matrix.index:
            # Cold start: recommend popular items
            return self.user_item_matrix.mean().sort_values(ascending=False).head(n).index.tolist()
        
        # Get items user hasn't rated
        user_ratings = self.user_item_matrix.loc[user_id]
        unrated_items = user_ratings[user_ratings.isna()].index
        
        # Predict ratings for unrated items
        predictions = {}
        for item_id in unrated_items:
            predictions[item_id] = self.predict(user_id, item_id)
        
        # Sort and return top N
        top_items = sorted(predictions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:n]
        return [item for item, score in top_items]

# Example usage
print("\nExample: User-Based CF")

# Create sample user-item matrix
data = {
    'Item1': [5, 4, np.nan, np.nan, 2],
    'Item2': [4, np.nan, 4, 5, 3],
    'Item3': [np.nan, 5, 5, 4, np.nan],
    'Item4': [2, 3, np.nan, 4, 4],
    'Item5': [5, np.nan, 4, np.nan, 5]
}
user_item = pd.DataFrame(data, index=['User1', 'User2', 'User3', 'User4', 'User5'])

print("\nUser-Item Matrix:")
print(user_item)

# Train model
cf = UserBasedCF(k=3)
cf.fit(user_item)

# Predict
user = 'User1'
item = 'Item3'
predicted = cf.predict(user, item)
print(f"\nPredicted rating for {user}, {item}: {predicted:.2f}")

# Recommend
recommendations = cf.recommend(user, n=3)
print(f"\nTop 3 recommendations for {user}: {recommendations}")
```

sections.title: Topic 205: Item-Based Collaborative Filtering
sections.body:
**Concept:**
"Users will like items similar to what they liked before"
- Find similar items
- Recommend items similar to what user liked

**Advantages over User-Based:**
✅ More stable (items change less than users)
✅ Faster for many users, few items
✅ Easier to explain

```python
class ItemBasedCF:
    """Item-Based Collaborative Filtering"""
    
    def __init__(self, k=5):
        self.k = k
        self.item_similarity = None
        self.user_item_matrix = None
    
    def fit(self, user_item_matrix):
        """Train: compute item similarity"""
        self.user_item_matrix = user_item_matrix
        
        # Transpose: items × users
        item_user_matrix = user_item_matrix.T
        
        # Compute item similarity
        self.item_similarity = cosine_similarity(item_user_matrix.fillna(0))
        
        self.item_similarity = pd.DataFrame(
            self.item_similarity,
            index=item_user_matrix.index,
            columns=item_user_matrix.index
        )
    
    def predict(self, user_id, item_id):
        """Predict rating"""
        if user_id not in self.user_item_matrix.index:
            return self.user_item_matrix[item_id].mean()
        
        if item_id not in self.user_item_matrix.columns:
            return self.user_item_matrix.loc[user_id].mean()
        
        # Get items user has rated
        user_ratings = self.user_item_matrix.loc[user_id].dropna()
        
        if len(user_ratings) == 0:
            return self.user_item_matrix[item_id].mean()
        
        # Get similarity to those items
        similar_items = self.item_similarity[item_id]
        similar_items = similar_items[similar_items.index.isin(user_ratings.index)]
        
        if len(similar_items) == 0:
            return self.user_item_matrix[item_id].mean()
        
        # Top k similar items
        top_k = similar_items.nlargest(self.k)
        
        # Weighted average
        weights = top_k.values
        ratings = user_ratings[top_k.index].values
        
        if weights.sum() == 0:
            return ratings.mean()
        
        predicted = np.dot(weights, ratings) / weights.sum()
        return predicted
    
    def recommend(self, user_id, n=10):
        """Get top N recommendations"""
        if user_id not in self.user_item_matrix.index:
            return self.user_item_matrix.mean().sort_values(ascending=False).head(n).index.tolist()
        
        user_ratings = self.user_item_matrix.loc[user_id]
        unrated_items = user_ratings[user_ratings.isna()].index
        
        predictions = {item: self.predict(user_id, item) for item in unrated_items}
        top_items = sorted(predictions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:n]
        
        return [item for item, score in top_items]

# Example
item_cf = ItemBasedCF(k=3)
item_cf.fit(user_item)

predicted = item_cf.predict('User1', 'Item3')
print(f"\nItem-Based CF prediction for User1, Item3: {predicted:.2f}")

recommendations = item_cf.recommend('User1', n=3)
print(f"Item-Based recommendations: {recommendations}")
```

sections.title: Topic 206: Matrix Factorization (Svd, Als)
sections.body:
**Concept:**
Decompose user-item matrix into latent factors
R ≈ U × I^T

where:
- R = rating matrix (m users × n items)
- U = user matrix (m users × k factors)
- I = item matrix (n items × k factors)

**Advantages:**
✅ Handles sparsity better
✅ Discovers latent features
✅ Scalable
✅ Works with implicit feedback

```python
# Matrix Factorization with Surprise library
print("\nMatrix Factorization with SVD:")

# Prepare data for Surprise
ratings_data = []
for user in user_item.index:
    for item in user_item.columns:
        rating = user_item.loc[user, item]
        if not np.isnan(rating):
            ratings_data.append([user, item, rating])

ratings_df = pd.DataFrame(ratings_data, columns=['user', 'item', 'rating'])

print("\nRatings DataFrame:")
print(ratings_df.head())

# Load data
reader = Reader(rating_scale=(1, 5))
data = Dataset.load_from_df(ratings_df, reader)

# Train SVD
algo = SVD(n_factors=10, n_epochs=20, lr_all=0.005, reg_all=0.02)

# Cross-validation
print("\nCross-validation:")
results = cross_validate(algo, data, measures=['RMSE', 'MAE'], cv=3, verbose=False)
print(f"RMSE: {results['test_rmse'].mean():.4f}")
print(f"MAE: {results['test_mae'].mean():.4f}")

# Train on full data
trainset = data.build_full_trainset()
algo.fit(trainset)

# Predict
pred = algo.predict('User1', 'Item3')
print(f"\nSVD prediction for User1, Item3: {pred.est:.2f}")

# Get top N recommendations
def get_top_n_svd(algo, user_id, user_item_matrix, n=5):
    """Get top N recommendations using trained SVD"""
    # Get all items
    all_items = user_item_matrix.columns
    
    # Get items user hasn't rated
    user_ratings = user_item_matrix.loc[user_id]
    unrated = user_ratings[user_ratings.isna()].index
    
    # Predict ratings
    predictions = [(item, algo.predict(user_id, item).est) for item in unrated]
    
    # Sort and return top N
    predictions.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    return predictions[:n]

top_n = get_top_n_svd(algo, 'User1', user_item, n=3)
print(f"\nTop 3 SVD recommendations for User1:")
for item, score in top_n:
    print(f"  {item}: {score:.2f}")
```

**Matrix Factorization Variants:**

1. SVD (Singular Value Decomposition):
- Explicit ratings
- Minimizes RMSE
- Good for rating prediction

2. NMF (Non-negative Matrix Factorization):
- Non-negative factors
- Interpretable latent features
- Good for implicit feedback

3. ALS (Alternating Least Squares):
- Scalable to large datasets
- Parallelizable
- Used in Spark MLlib

4. Bayesian Personalized Ranking (BPR):
- For implicit feedback
- Learns pairwise preferences
- Good for top-N recommendations

**Comparison:**
┌────────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐
│ Method         │ User-Based   │ Item-Based   │ Matrix Fact  │
├────────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┤
│ Scalability    │ Low          │ Medium       │ High         │
│ Sparsity       │ Poor         │ Better       │ Best         │
│ Cold Start     │ Poor         │ Poor         │ Medium       │
│ Explainability │ Good         │ Best         │ Low          │
│ Accuracy       │ Medium       │ Medium       │ High         │
└────────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┘

sections.title: Topic 207: Content-Based Filtering
sections.body:
**Concept:**
Recommend items similar to what user liked before
Based on item features/attributes

**Steps:**
1. Extract item features
2. Build item profiles
3. Build user profiles from liked items
4. Recommend similar items

**Advantages:**
✅ No cold start for items
✅ Can recommend niche items
✅ Explainable recommendations

**Disadvantages:**
❌ Limited to user's history
❌ No serendipity
❌ Requires feature engineering

```python
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity

class ContentBasedRecommender:
    """Content-Based Recommender using TF-IDF"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.tfidf = TfidfVectorizer(stop_words='english')
        self.item_profiles = None
        self.item_similarity = None
        self.items_df = None
    
    def fit(self, items_df, text_column):
        """
        Fit recommender on item descriptions.
        
        items_df: DataFrame with item_id and text features
        text_column: name of column with text descriptions
        """
        self.items_df = items_df
        
        # Create TF-IDF vectors for items
        self.item_profiles = self.tfidf.fit_transform(items_df[text_column])
        
        # Compute item similarity matrix
        self.item_similarity = cosine_similarity(self.item_profiles)
        
        return self
    
    def get_similar_items(self, item_id, n=10):
        """Find items similar to given item"""
        idx = self.items_df[self.items_df['item_id'] == item_id].index[0]
        
        # Get similarity scores
        sim_scores = list(enumerate(self.item_similarity[idx]))
        
        # Sort by similarity
        sim_scores = sorted(sim_scores, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        
        # Get top n (excluding the item itself)
        sim_scores = sim_scores[1:n+1]
        
        # Get item indices
        item_indices = [i[0] for i in sim_scores]
        
        return self.items_df.iloc[item_indices]['item_id'].tolist()
    
    def recommend(self, user_liked_items, n=10):
        """
        Recommend items based on user's liked items.
        
        user_liked_items: list of item_ids user liked
        n: number of recommendations
        """
        # Get similar items for each liked item
        all_similar = []
        for item_id in user_liked_items:
            similar = self.get_similar_items(item_id, n=20)
            all_similar.extend(similar)
        
        # Count occurrences (items similar to multiple liked items are better)
        from collections import Counter
        item_counts = Counter(all_similar)
        
        # Remove already liked items
        for item in user_liked_items:
            if item in item_counts:
                del item_counts[item]
        
        # Get top n
        top_items = [item for item, count in item_counts.most_common(n)]
        return top_items

# Example: Movie recommendations
print("\nExample: Content-Based Movie Recommendations")

movies = pd.DataFrame({
    'item_id': ['m1', 'm2', 'm3', 'm4', 'm5'],
    'title': ['The Matrix', 'Inception', 'Titanic', 'The Notebook', 'Interstellar'],
    'description': [
        'sci-fi action virtual reality computer hacker',
        'sci-fi thriller dream layers subconscious',
        'romance drama ship disaster love story',
        'romance drama love story memory',
        'sci-fi space travel time dilation father daughter'
    ]
})

print("\nMovies:")
print(movies[['item_id', 'title']])

# Train content-based recommender
cb_rec = ContentBasedRecommender()
cb_rec.fit(movies, 'description')

# User liked The Matrix
user_liked = ['m1']  # The Matrix
recommendations = cb_rec.recommend(user_liked, n=3)

print(f"\nUser liked: {movies[movies['item_id']=='m1']['title'].values[0]}")
print("Recommendations:")
for item_id in recommendations:
    title = movies[movies['item_id']==item_id]['title'].values[0]
    print(f"  - {title}")
```

sections.title: Topic 208: Hybrid Recommender Systems
sections.body:
**Concept:**
Combine multiple recommendation techniques

**Types of Hybrid:**
1. Weighted: Combine scores from different methods
2. Switching: Switch between methods based on context
3. Mixed: Present results from multiple methods
4. Feature Combination: Use CF features in content-based
5. Cascade: Refine recommendations progressively
6. Feature Augmentation: Use one method's output as feature for another
7. Meta-level: Use one method to train another

**Benefits:**
✅ Better accuracy
✅ Handles cold start
✅ Increases diversity
✅ More robust

```python
class HybridRecommender:
    """Hybrid Recommender: Weighted combination of CF + Content-Based"""
    
    def __init__(self, cf_model, cb_model, cf_weight=0.5):
        self.cf_model = cf_model
        self.cb_model = cb_model
        self.cf_weight = cf_weight
        self.cb_weight = 1 - cf_weight
    
    def recommend(self, user_id, user_liked_items, n=10):
        """
        Hybrid recommendations.
        
        user_id: for collaborative filtering
        user_liked_items: for content-based filtering
        """
        # Get CF recommendations
        try:
            cf_recs = self.cf_model.recommend(user_id, n=n*2)
        except:
            cf_recs = []
        
        # Get content-based recommendations
        try:
            cb_recs = self.cb_model.recommend(user_liked_items, n=n*2)
        except:
            cb_recs = []
        
        # Combine with weights
        scores = {}
        
        for item in cf_recs:
            scores[item] = scores.get(item, 0) + self.cf_weight
        
        for item in cb_recs:
            scores[item] = scores.get(item, 0) + self.cb_weight
        
        # Sort and return top n
        top_items = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:n]
        return [item for item, score in top_items]

# Example
print("\nHybrid Recommender Example:")
hybrid_rec = HybridRecommender(item_cf, cb_rec, cf_weight=0.6)

# This would combine both methods
print("Hybrid recommendations combine:")
print("  60% Collaborative Filtering (what similar users liked)")
print("  40% Content-Based (items similar to what you liked)")
```

sections.title: Topic 209: Cold Start Problem
sections.body:
**Problem:**
- New Users: No history → Can't use CF
- New Items: No ratings → Can't recommend

**Solutions:**

1. For New Users:
✅ Ask preferences during onboarding
✅ Recommend popular items
✅ Use demographic info
✅ Show diverse items to learn quickly
✅ Use content-based on selected items

2. For New Items:
✅ Use content-based features
✅ Cold start as exploration (multi-armed bandit)
✅ Leverage item metadata
✅ Cross-domain recommendations

3. Hybrid Approaches:
✅ Start with content-based
✅ Gradually incorporate CF
✅ Use knowledge-based recommendations

```python
class ColdStartHandler:
    """Handle cold start for new users and items"""
    
    def __init__(self, popular_items, content_based_model=None):
        self.popular_items = popular_items
        self.content_based_model = content_based_model
    
    def recommend_new_user(self, n=10):
        """Recommend to brand new user (no history)"""
        # Start with most popular items
        return self.popular_items[:n]
    
    def recommend_after_onboarding(self, selected_items, n=10):
        """Recommend after user selects a few items"""
        if self.content_based_model:
            # Use content-based on selected items
            return self.content_based_model.recommend(selected_items, n)
        else:
            # Fall back to popular items
            return self.popular_items[:n]
    
    def handle_new_item(self, new_item_features):
        """Handle new item with no ratings"""
        if self.content_based_model:
            # Find similar items based on content
            similar = self.content_based_model.get_similar_items(new_item_features, n=5)
            return similar
        return []
```

**Cold Start Best Practices:**
1. Collect explicit preferences early
2. Use contextual information (location, time, device)
3. Leverage social connections
4. Apply active learning (ask strategic questions)
5. Use multi-armed bandit algorithms (explore vs exploit)
6. Bootstrap from external data sources
